attack_mechanism: Holding or toggling `openMSP430.cpuoff` at a completion boundary can repeatedly withdraw the condition that releases the instruction state machine. Debug halt and low-power controls can hold the frontend in `I_IDLE`/`E_IDLE` or delay the boundary at which a running instruction completes. `openMSP430.cpuoff` controls that halt/resume path before `exec_done` is consumed by decode and fetch; the active mux/state branches are selected by `openMSP430.cpuoff`, `openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_jmp`. Signal propagation follows `openMSP430.cpuoff -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_first_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state_nxt -> openMSP430.frontend_0.e_state -> openMSP430.frontend_0.exec_done`. Legitimate instructions cease retiring and the processor remains halted or repeatedly re-enters an incomplete execution phase.
